en: The Monk Fǎxiān, a Dharma-heir of the late Master Gǔlín, composed this preface for the *Collected Omitted Verses and Hymns*.
Attended by his junior disciple, the attendant Hǎishòu, he once brought a large volume and said to me: "Yesterday, there was the Venerable Rúwén."
He intended to travel south to seek instruction, so he boarded a merchant ship and departed. A gale blew them to Tamra, where the vessel was wrecked.
He remained stranded in Goryeo. When the people of Goryeo asked him the reason for his presence there, he produced a massive volume to show them;
it consisted entirely of the works of National Preceptor Goeun, with only one or two brief interludes concerning National Preceptor Dongshan Kong. Upon hearing this, they recorded it.
He considered that he had obtained a precious treasure and was returning home. This year, another ship set sail;
he then left it with his senior brother Xuánshī Jùchāng, and subsequently traveled south again. Thereupon, Xuánshī requested it on behalf of the Master.
Furthermore, he remarked, "Upon examination, these are all among the works carved and recorded by the ancestral master Gǔlín; for the most part, there is nothing new here. Xuánshī then recorded them.
I have brought forth those works which had not yet been published; whenever an opportunity arose, I published them.

Although these were items discarded by my own master and ancestors—much like a bright pearl or a large shell cast away by a wealthy householder—a poor man who finds them may enjoy their benefits without end.
I said, "What you say is true. However, as for my poverty, I do not desire bright pearls or large shells; I shall simply follow what you prefer.
Shou replied again, "This manuscript copy has many omissions and errors, particularly severe. I hope you will collate it.
I said, "How can one know what the original composition was like in order to collate it? This is a great difficulty. Nevertheless—"
I strongly acceded to your request. Thereupon, Shou compiled them and collated them;

in instances where characters were missing or erroneous, as I could not ascertain what the actual words might have been, I supplied them based on my own judgment. Thus, I obtained two hundred and ninety-four verses.
Later, the attendant Xuanyu came from the Nine Provinces and, upon seeing them, said: "My [collection] is identical to that of Ruwen."
Chiji obtained this manuscript in Goryeo. Thinking, "How can I not immediately carve the printing blocks?
he wished to solicit donations and requested that I compose a preface. I declined, whereupon he asked Jianren, and subsequently approached the Tripitaka Master Yuanshu.
I obtained thirty-nine verses, as well as five titles and colophons from the head seat Daojiao.
I had them collated with one another, and wherever there were points requiring interrogation, I provided annotations on the spot. An ancient proverb says: "Collating books is like sweeping away dust;
it can never be fully accomplished. How much more so in this case, where there is no original text to verify against? Furthermore, is it not also due to my own inadequacy? No.
It is simply not exhausted; it must also have been made largely of gold and silver carriages. May those who see this not mock it.
Written in the autumn of the year Kōei-otoshi (1365) at the East Pavilion of the East Hall in Nansen-ji.
Donor for the Auxiliary Conditions:
Before His Majesty the Emperor,
the Great Dharma Sovereign, Fujiwara no Tadamichi, Acting Grand Counselor.
The Counselor-in-Chief, Genjūshi,
and the Councilor, Fujiwara Kishin,
[visit] the Nyorai-zō-in Palace.
From the two ladies,
Fujiwara Ukon-in and Ichijō-no-tenshi Genjūko.
Supplementary Verses and Eulogies of Master Gulin, Volume One.
Compiled by the Bhikṣu Haishou from the Sayings of Reading Ying’an.
The old man of Heiyun is a lump of deluded flesh; three hundred years have passed, yet his warmth remains. Among the myriad blossoms of the human world, their colors are now withering;
yet within the cave, this single branch of red has not changed. The Yellow River breaks its banks as leviathans roar; Mount Taihua collapses as the Great Spirit flees.
Do not boast of high-handed skills for slaying dragons; first see how he bites pigs and dogs. From the southern heavens to the northern earth...
A realm without discursive thought—neither lingering in the level nor grasping at the precipitous. With a snap of the fingers, eighty thousand gates open into emptiness;
the white hare and red crow depart toward the west.
*Farewell to Elder Cui Feng as he departs for the Capital.*
He did not see Emperor Tongguang; having recovered the Central Plains was not yet considered noble. Vast and boundless within the seas, no one knew it;
though the supreme treasure had been obtained, who would look upon it? Xinghua briefly lent it for a view: its radiance illuminates heaven and earth.
He lifts up the hem of his head-wrap, revealing a golden arm. One does not see Emperor Song Taizong parting from the monk amidst the spiritual mountains—three thousand [miles].
The words of the inscription may be verified. Beneath the Shadowless Tree, a golden dragon coils; today’s Son of Heaven surpasses him even further.

This is the Heart-Teaching of our Buddha, spoken from his own mouth. Through the sagely culture and divine martial prowess of the three or four kings, the mountains and rivers of the great earth stand in awe of their heroic majesty.

Those on the left and right are all like Gao and Kui; throughout the eight directions, everyone is like Houji and Xie. Once the customs have returned to their original purity, how could my Way not be brilliantly manifest?

The Great State Preceptor, who received the empowerment upon his crown, has received the prediction of enlightenment one by one. Do not sleep soundly while cherishing Lake Dongting; every step you take is precisely the time to go to court at the Golden Gate.
Cast aside that which is to the left of East Mountain; this is the moment when the absolute reality is revealed to the naked eye.

Seeing off a monk returning to Tiantai to visit his retired teacher, I spoke this verse without regard for tonal prosody. Pierced here and there, it lies in utter disarray. The lightning-fast pivot of the mind is difficult to conceive;
let go from within emptiness, as straight as a taut string. Moreover, since the Buddha-dharma has no fixed period, who can fathom its wondrous function, free in all directions?
"I understand. It may well be that the blue sky covers the white sun, yet the dust at the bottom of the well cannot fly upward.

This man of the Way was born on Mount Tiantai; his character and bearing are remarkably spiritual and extraordinary. Having braved the heat to come and knock at my door, he sought a verse for his journey.

Now, returning to his master’s side, he recounts it word for word from beginning to end: 'Clouds rise on the Southern Mountain, rain falls on the Northern Mountain; traveling east, one sees no benefit in traveling west.'"
Seeing off a Monk for Mount Wutai: Mount Wutai is the Land of Coolness; within its mountains all is of golden hue. Amidst layered mists and clouds, no person is seen;
it is said that Mañjuśrī emerges halfway up the heavens. In years past, Asaṅga knew nothing of this; now the Buddha-dharma has flourished in the South.
How could three hundred or five hundred be considered too few? The first three and the last three are even more extraordinary. To this day, the count in our eyes remains insufficient;
we see only green mountains and secluded valleys. Where the golden oriole cries, white clouds fly; when the lion roars, the fragrant grasses turn green.
You, Master, belong naturally to the lineage of Hanshan and Shide; you have suddenly set out on a journey to Mount Tai. Your divine radiance...

Ten thousand *li* away, his forehead is bare; he wears a single garment of coarse cloth, his eyes a pair of azure. Sentient beings, tormented by feverish afflictions, long for the nectar of immortality;
the gate of great giving has opened to spread it abroad. On another day, he will let go of his hand from the precipice and return home—do not say that east and west have been left unentrusted.
"Where the golden oriole cries, white clouds fly; when the lion roars, the green grasses flourish.
If one were to take this from the perspective of a poet, might it not be called an extraordinary verse? Yet, this is not poetry.

Furthermore, regarding these two lines, while people can easily recite the first four characters—"Where the golden oriole cries" and "When the lion roars"—the subsequent three characters, "white clouds fly" and "green grasses flourish," are difficult to connect [to the preceding].
Above this, who could possibly emulate it?
Following the rhyme of Master Yunwai, I send off Chan Master Wan:
"From of old, a single drop of Caoxi’s water; its swirling waves rise from level ground. The man of the Way has long possessed the power to cut across the stream."

The pivot of opportunity: the power to haul back the Celestial River is such as this. Casting a golden hook from the summit of Incense Burner Peak, one catches a crimson carp before the Heron’s Nest Pavilion.
At night, the preaching in the celestial palace leaves dreams at rest; the wondrous principle of the four lines and hundred negations is empty.

This single taboo that strikes head-on cannot be touched; the three fists beneath the ribs can never be compared. Hiding the body within the Big Dipper, the five ranks are divided; a blink of the eye—white.
Clouds stretch for thousands of miles; this morning you came to visit me east of the river. On the riverbank, the spring breeze is just now awakening the peach and plum blossoms.
In an instant, we spoke our farewells and departed in haste. The green mud beneath your feet remains entirely unwashed.
In the same rhyme as before, I send this to my old friend in Dongzhou:
"Rice in the bowl, water in the bucket—whence did this saying arise? Among the pivotal devices of the seventeen hundred patriarchs, which device first structured this?
Cease dwelling in anger; lift up the hanging goiter in the void. Inquire after the Red Ox of those years."
The carp leaps at the treetops; though heaven is high and earth is deep, it hears nothing at last. Under twenty li of pines we discuss the wondrous principle:

not a speck of dust remains, and the myriad realms are at peace. How can bright moon and clear breeze compare? Gazing at the flying geese from the eastern bank of the Chu River, my hometown lies at the far end of the Blue Sea.
When shall I take up my single staff and ride the surging waves, sharing a single platter upon the rocks to chew red plums? Laughing until I fall over!
This old man Qici on the street: the waters of the Ning River are so limpid they are as pure as if washed clean.
To the Vinaya Master Ning:
you would rather let your body be shattered into fine dust than ever again blind the eyes of a sentient being. I laugh at that Huangbo, acting like such a doting old woman.
The mind—how is it like Muzhou carrying a single board? He split open the Three Essentials and the Three Mysteries, and raised high the eye atop the crown of Maheśvara.
"Go back! Go back! As the curtain rolls up, the spring day in the Western Mountains is long; where the thin mist stretches across, the peaks stand revealed in their majesty.
It would be better for Yichuan to fall ill so that he might entrust himself [to the truth].
There was once a man whose skin adhered to his bones; unable to remove it, he wandered the streets seeking medicine to eat. Yichuan, too, frequently ran to physicians’ houses.
His illness could not be cured, for the medicine lacked efficacy. Xueyan’s whole body is festering pus; Caoshan seeks the point of origin.

It is not permitted. To carry medical texts and store medicines while hearing of the monastic communities—though today, even after a hundred ailments have attacked me, I have realized that the four great elements are originally empty.
It was for the sake of sentient beings that I manifested this illness; one should know that Vimalakīrti’s words were also spoken out of necessity.
Ultimately, when the body is at peace, the Way is truly fulfilled. I now joyfully recite this gāthā to swiftly eliminate the tumor upon my crown. [To all] in the ten directions...
The Bodhisattvas bear witness together to the Mahāprajñāpāramitā.
I am sending this Chan practitioner to Dongshan in Dongchan to transcribe the wild geese at the edge of the sky;
yet their plumage is not true, and thus the task remains unaccomplished. Was it perhaps that his skill was lacking in those days?

Alas! To marry a wife without money is like carrying a single board; to wish to paint a "Western Herdsman" while living in retirement is to have arms and hands lacking strength and eyes and brain coarse.
Comparing the present with the past, all are exactly like this; they hand it over to patch-robed monks to compete for fame and style.

With arms folded by a cliff, one sits in broad daylight; facing one’s own shadow, two distinct figures are formed. Because one watches the crows fighting over their nests in the treetops, one does not even know where one’s own head is.
Falling from the heights into the red dust, the old Dharma-brother of Dongchan merely laughs at me when he opens his mouth: "In the Buddha-dharma, I have not an inch of growth;
I only know how to swallow grains of rice. One day, when you see King Yama, he will shove you onto an iron bed to lie upon. Alas for the Buddha!
Let him release me so that my belly may grow large.
Two Poems on Recalling Master Fan Zhūsu, the Head of the Academy at Tiānmén, on an Autumn Day At dawn I gaze upon the green mountains, as the rising sun illuminates the empty walls.
The noble personage atop Gūxī Hill ascends the honored seat to lecture and guide us.

The enlightened age prizes outstanding talent; you, Wen, are the legitimate heir of this lineage. Throughout your life, you have harbored the ambitions of a great man; your only concern was that your heart might not be as firm as stone.
First sorrowful, then finally joyful—such a state has rarely been encountered in a thousand years. You are like a bright mirror within its case, or a shimmering jade gem from Mount Jing.
The mirror compares with the hearts of men of antiquity; the jade disc embodies the virtue of a noble gentleman. Thus, throughout heaven and earth, though one seeks it, it cannot be found.
How deep my longing, how deep indeed! When shall I behold its countenance?

I recall our parting beneath the walls of Wu City; my heart has wandered aimlessly for a thousand li. I grieve that you are engaged in official service, as the mountains and rivers wind and intertwine before you.
Literary composition is but a minor art; how can it compare to the wisdom of the enlightened? Having finished lecturing on the scriptures at dawn, I wander together with the students.
I have troubled you with my frequent visits by the Guchui River; in haste, I have become a lingering guest. An autumn wind rises from the courtyard trees, and a crescent moon shines upon the roof.
In the vast sky there are only migrating geese; across the level plains, no boat finds mooring. Is it not that I have something on my mind? Yet there is no way to send a poem to express it.
How long it has been! How long indeed! When shall we finally return to the forest retreats?
I am uncertain regarding the character "脫" (tuō) and do not dare to arbitrarily fill in the gap.
Sent to the monk-prefect Zhang at Funing Prefecture, Lin Guyan.
The Dharma-path of Zhongwu is acclaimed throughout the world; Ju Chi is a preeminent talent among the clergy.

For three years he served as an assistant at Guyan, where he categorized documents and records with effortless ease. Tiantai has long been a land of refined culture, concealing its excellence and producing spiritual wonders.
As the autumn moon is still bright and the autumn waters are clear, there was never any duality in the Master’s mind. This is the renowned prefecture of Funing.
Between mountain valleys, tidal fields grow rice to provide for the banquet; the customs are pure and the people thick with virtue as the Sage’s transformation spreads.

Pagodas are arrayed like chess pieces, circling like the stars. A purple steed, its frost-white hooves light, gallops forth; the curtains are drawn aside along the road as the people welcome him with joy.
Holding the bronze seal in his grasp, he spreads his reputation for good governance; let us wait to see him soar upon the ten-thousand-li journey of the Peng bird.
I send Xiangyi Cloud to Wuxian as an assistant head of the administrative office;

serenely, a single expanse of Western Mountain clouds unfurls and rolls within the realm beyond the mundane, bringing forth the blossoms of spring. With a solemn heart toward the ancestral Way, I look for the rain;

may it thoroughly moisten the parched and withered for us anew. In human life, how could one’s worth lie in the nobility of the "five horses"? To protect the Dharma and bring peace to the Sangha—this is true value.
Easy. Behold the time when the essential principles flourish most: Along the roads, crowds vie to welcome the arrival of the Star of Fortune.
At Hengtang, willow buds sway in the clear ripples; The sound of rhythmic singing pierces through the cries of the orioles. With coins in hand, they buy wine to share in conviviality.
I wish to emulate the old man of Duling in years past, Forgetting all formalities of "you" and "I" with you, sir.
In sending off Dao-master Dai, I say:

The purity of severed clouds and the crystalline clarity of an ice pitcher are not sufficient for true purity; the brilliance of a precious mirror reflecting the soul is not sufficient for true brilliance.

For three years, Dao-master Dai has presided over the district of Wu; as bright as a solitary moon suspended in the azure heavens, the Dharma-way of the Southeast is as vast as this. How [could it ever be exhausted]?
A man exerts himself to uphold the principles of order, casting all fame and achievement aside as trivial. Little does he know that the Creator favors his talent and beauty;
their deep affection and profound loyalty exceed even the firmness of metal and stone. Grasping the reins, he inquires with earnest care after his travels;

upon hearing it said that his former name from the Three Mountains is still known to many, he reflects: "How late has the dew and rain from the heavens arrived? Clouds, by nature, have no intention to part."
The sequence continues: "Another day, when you gallop your horse through the golden gates, we shall again pour *ling-lu* wine together under the fragrant breeze.
The former Abbot Gu gave me a *bèi-yè* (palm leaf) manuscript to show me;

this high personage presented me with a *bèituó-yè* (pātra-leaf) that had come from Zhugan (India), its brilliance shining brightly. When I first looked at the Sanskrit script, the ink was still fresh.
How fresh! Their arrangements, whether horizontal or diagonal, do not overlap. Reflecting back on the time of the First Council, who among the true sons of the Dharma King could have known this?
Ānanda, though free from further learning, possessed only a powerful memory; Kāśyapa remained silent with his brows ever furrowed.

Even the mother by the eastern city gate had no desire to see the Buddha—how could she have recognized this as something marvelous? Now, as I join my palms in reverence, my faculty of mind is awakened from its long slumber.

How can habitual tendencies be eliminated? Like flowers in the sky that have no root, yet one attempts to produce fruit. By parsing the lines and reading the verses, the ignorance within the chest is opened.

For those born late to study the Way, diligence is precious; the Red Water has a bottom, so one should seek the pearl therein. In a mere moment the high person departs again, like trying to stop a small child’s incessant crying.
The Honored Guest, a seeker of the Way from Gusu, has arrived. When did he leave Fufou? Our meeting fills me with a profound melancholy; we sit in silence, utterly still.
After a long while, his countenance relaxes, and he casts off the burdens within his breast. Once the things within the breast are gone, there remains only true gold. A hundred...
Refining the scriptures in a crimson furnace; at the ten-thousand-fathom Dragon Gate, one dreads a mere spot on the forehead. A single probe into the tiger’s den leaves no trace of the *shu-tu*.

Yangqi’s donkey has three legs; it gallops across heaven and earth, boasting of its own strategy. Letting go and gathering back upon the tips of a hundred blades of grass—upright four, horizontal three—it cannot be grasped.
In an instant, you depart from me; where will you return? With sleeves full of paper, I wish to write a long-short poem.
Whether short or long, one should examine it for oneself; whether right or wrong, they are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
This was presented to Zheng Gongzhi.
When Gongzhi formerly resided in Gusu, his reputation was far-reaching and everyone alike esteemed him; his perilous words and blunt arguments were comparable to those of the ancients.
The Sage is like a sharp awl thrust from its sheath; once he was honored and distinguished in Gusu, how many times since have I looked back as the moon fades and the stars wane?
Ten thousand miles away, the clouds part and his noble wings soar high; with a single roar of thunder, the great whale bellows forth. For a man to stand alone in this world is difficult;
facing the wind, I raise my voice in three sighs of emptiness. My schemes are sparse and my plans clumsy—I cannot fathom myself—yet I turn my back on fame and cherish [the Way].
Virtuous companions harm one another; the western wind blows leaf by leaf against the ruined walls. Elbows bare and robes tattered, my eyes cannot bear to look.
I hear it said that woven lotus leaves can ward off the cold; I shall borrow the power of a needle’s point to aid my hands.
I suspect that the character "eye" (眼) may actually be "sleep" (眠).

The Abbot Yu styled himself as the "Daoist Man of Lia'an," naming his hermitage after the character "Liao. This is precisely to share the same realization as the Buddhas and Patriarchs; even now, all myriad thoughts have already ceased.

Extinction—how could it wait for hands to be joined before being fully understood? Each person possesses their own treasury of luminosity; with a single blow of the hammer, both parts are resolved at once.
If one uses discrimination to forcibly fashion a mold, then sight, form, sound, and hearing are all but delusions.

What is within the hermitage and what is outside the hermitage—if there is a deviation of even a hair’s breadth, one loses a thousand miles. Rolling through the fields, appearing and disappearing as they will in every direction—they make even the gods Shen and Tu laugh to their downfall.
Together with Yulei, the supreme person above all cannot be grasped through deliberation. The empty void is difficult to compare even to the Great Void.
One must directly bring affairs to an end before resting; do not come to dwell in this hermitage until you have done so.
This master’s name is Qingyu. His natural disposition was exceedingly pure. His preceptor was Chan Master Fuyu of Huyan at Mount Jing;
he also served at Mount Jing for a long time, following the Elder Gulín, from whom he received dharma transmission as his successor.
He emerged into the public monastic world at Kaifú in Piaoshui, subsequently resided at Benjué, and now occupies the Eastern Hall.
The Founding Patriarch left behind a single sandal for the monks; it has been broadcast to the ears of people for ten thousand ages.
The Old Man of Dongshan, eyes covered in rheum, goes day after day for thousands of *li* barefoot upon his shoulders. Whether one steps upon it or not, it is all one's own. Vast and expansive!
The tradition of this lineage must be upheld with vigor. Its wondrous spiritual powers transcend words and meanings. To plant melon sprouts upon a stone—this was a saying of Fachang:
"He has tied together a large winter gourd; though a swift axe strikes, it cannot be split. It cuts off the throats of the monks;
take it for certain, three or five of them. A-he-he! Do you understand?
Submitted to the Compassionate Head Preceptor:
The Buddha-dharma is like the moon in the water; the Yellow-Faced Gautama spoke it with his own mouth. How, indeed, is the karmic consciousness of sentient beings?
They pursue shadows and follow forms, engaging in false discrimination. An old man dwells therein at Qin-chuan; one mind and three contemplations are both present.
Perfectly interfused: empty space is the mouth, the myriad phenomena are the tongue. To every visitor, one by one, he opens the eyes of the blind and the ears of the deaf.
In the four quarters, breezes sweep away as fragrant winds waft; withered flowers have fallen away, and fresh blossoms glow red. Do not allow yellow leaves to fall before the steps;
they would obscure the tracks of those coming and going among devas and humans.
At the western side of the *vīnā*’s dwelling place, thorns grow regardless of the ground.
When spring arrives, they bloom of their own accord. On what day will the sandalwood trees be planted? Few people come to the forest retreat.
Where are Xiangnan and Tanbei? The clouds are deep, the paths are remote, and the mountains are steep and lofty.

Once a man has realized everything that needs to be realized, what does the Buddha-dharma have to do with him? Have you not seen how Master Mazu said, "Mind itself is Buddha," and under these words, Daimei attained sudden enlightenment?
Yet when he later said, "Neither mind nor Buddha," it was very much like piling up bones on level ground. Since this is so—

Encountering such delusion and confusion, what prevents one from being like a duck hearing thunder? Wandering on Mount Nanyue in the morning and heading to Mount Tiantai in the evening—just go like this;
when will you ever return?
To Liu Liwen of Dànzhāi, a paragon among scholars and a hero among monks:
his reputation is vast and grand, restoring our school. Since Master Pei and Old Pang have long since passed away, who can aspire to emulate their lofty style?
The round fruit has finally formed upon the iron tree; it is a wondrous species from a divine root.
Yet it is distinct: no branches, no leaves, just bare red twigs. I have heard that the flowers bloom in the twelfth month;
at Caoxi, the waves are deep and cold. The clear river flows forth like a rushing torrent; the old fisherman stands back, not daring to enter, dropping a green *lang-jan* gem from his hand.
My household livelihood you already know; beyond a single punch, what else can be done? On another day...
Meeting him, there is no need to unfasten the belt at the waist; Master Shu’s hand and face possess swift and sharp spiritual acuity.
Sending off a monk to return to Yandang:
all Buddhas do not show their heads, and the Patriarchs have no handle to grasp. Even Mahānārāyaṇa, of great strength, cannot lift his own raised foot.
The superior man is like a colt of the heavenly steeds; his galloping is such as this. At every turn, life and death are chillingly manifest; at every stroke, he transcends words and meaning.
Only then does one see the wind and thunder arise, followed immediately by the arrival of the thunderclap. Cease dwelling in clever artifices; upon meeting, simply cover your ears.
Seeing him spared from three days of deafness, it was better to lose a momentary profit than gain it. Reflecting on the divine traces and numinous wonders of Nāgārjuna:
where waterfalls cascade over cliffs, he would kneel and simply doze off; he feared neither the shock of dragons nor crocodiles, seeing only the fear of his fellow monastics.
In the past, I struck him with a single blow of my fist and knocked out two of his teeth. At that time, he was merely struck senseless; there was nothing else remarkable about it.
If we were to meet today, I would simply bow my head in prostration. This is not a matter of physical strength or power; how much less so for one who is a disciple of the Buddha?
Seeing off a monk departing for Yongjia:
he neither leaps over the vajra-ring nor can he swallow the chestnut thorn. Thirsty he drinks and hungry he eats, passing his days in such a manner;
how could he know there is another true message? You, Master, are fortunately a native of Dongjia; do not take the Buddha-dharma as...
Human nature: when the patched robe is stripped away, one receives a severe blow. If there were eyes on the tip of the staff, we would surely have known each other;
yet the Old Man Dajue was truly a blind thief. Xinghua had words, yet he still lacked virtue. The intent of our former teacher was originally not much;

how could it have been obtained through the power of Huangbo? Who dares speak of the golden mallet within his sleeve? Above the crown of the head, there is yet a "heaven-penetrating" aperture. Tell this to...
The Master who stayed but one night at Caoqi—before the river moon and pine winds, he must have been struck with laughter.
I see off a monk from Chuanshou traveling to Tiantai;
this man of the Way came all the way from Xichuan, yet now rolls up his robes to speak of returning to Tiantai. The green peaks of Tiantai and Xichuan are but a thousand-fold distance apart.
A village. Wandering by morning and arriving by evening—truly leisurely! Such is the wondrous power of supernatural penetration.
Fenggan and Shide are truly worthy companions. Singing several songs, the cliff-side rocks split; performing a brief dance, the mountain flowers bloom with a laugh.

When the mountain flowers bloom, they fill the crags and valleys. Who would say that the Master’s wanderings are not enough? To the south of the Stone Bridge is the aged Tanyou; meeting him, one is surely...
Inviting Fangguang to stay overnight: A patch-robed monk possesses a single pair of heavenly eyes; they do not reside on the eyebrows or the temples.
Pure, penetrating, and luminous, they are at the crown of the head, shining brilliantly, illuminating heaven and earth. Half a catty is eight ounces—there is no difference in height.
Through all eternity, who has ever seen them intimately? If one suddenly touches the tip of their own nose, they can immediately open up a single thread for others.
Since it is clearly manifest at the crown of the head, why does one’s awareness remain upon the tip of the nose? I shall walk through the wild weeds;
you must not follow. If you should walk there, you will be entangled by the grass. Have you not seen Ma Boji of Jiangxi? How could he ever have lacked salt and sauce in his reckless conduct?
The character "cui" (翠) is also questionable. Furthermore, the rhymes in the latter part are also very loose.
Regarding the two poems shown to the monks:
"Speech and silence transcend verbal explanation; seeing and hearing go beyond sound and form. As soon as Master Ma ascended the hall, Baizhang came forward and rolled up the mat.

The souls and spirits of the ten thousand phenomena are struck with awe; the void itself leans its two ears toward them. Like lightning rolling and stars racing, this is a mechanism beyond the conventional;

like heaven turning and earth revolving, it is the power of spiritual penetration (*ṛddhi*). To set aside Mount Sumeru and swallow the ridge of the Buddha hall—take it for granted that the true lineage flows from within the house.
Let people call it the "thief of ignorance. The white-fanged tiger of the Southern Mountain crouches there, unrecognized by anyone. Bite him to death!
The great beast—its roar and radiance resound everywhere. Splitting open the summit of the Three Mysteries, I gaze upward; its seven holes and eight apertures fill my heart and breast.

It has been long since I ceased dwelling in indolence; in this old house of but a few rafters, I have remained alone for a long time. As for the gruel and rice, I do not choose between the refined and the coarse.
Coarse! In the ways of the world, who else can distinguish beauty from ugliness? Before the crags, a sleeping tiger does not answer the call; atop the ridges, white clouds beckon as companions.
In the square pond, the sun warms the water-fowl as they fly; along the secluded path, the grass grows deep where the lion roars. The Master has come from afar from Mount Zhongfeng;
his two piercing eyes shoot forth like stars across the Ox and Dipper constellations. He draws his precious sword and brandishes it before him; he scatters divine pearls.
He strides toward the center of the mandala; how marvelous! He profoundly clarifies the mechanism beyond the formal teachings. Standing out prominently, he refuses to fall behind others.
When he sits with great authority upon the high seat in the future, he shall give me a thorough scolding as an old man from Mount Zhongfeng.
This was certainly composed while he was residing at the stupa of the ancestral master Xuyun (Lungzhu) on Mount Huqiu. Later, when he showed it to the Chan practitioner Yun, the same was true.
Because the Master had retired from Kaiyuan Temple, Chan Master Yong of Dongzhou invited him; they served as both host and guest in turn to welcome those coming from all quarters.
For this reason, aspiring monastics flocked there like ants drawn to honey. Consequently, there was later another recluse who came to Yunyan;
his poetic debts numbered in the thousands and tens of thousands, for from the beginning of the year to its end, he would write with a swift hand verses whose meanings were indistinguishable.
To Chan Master Chao:
Stones run and sand flies as the year draws to a close. You, O Chan practitioner, have come seeking a parting verse. On Vulture Peak there is a profound saying;
ultimately, who is the true heir? It is not the "thorny chestnut," nor is it the "diamond circle. Lake Tai.
Thirty-six thousand *qǐng*. The Yellow River has been clear and transparent for three thousand years. The point of inquiry does not lie upon the tip of the tongue;
do not come to sell water by the riverbank. Why is it so? It is not worth half a coin.
At first, I merely intended to compose a four-line metrical structure; however, I subsequently altered and extended it to form this ancient-style verse.
Presented to the practitioner Ciyun.
A single phrase cuts off the flow; heaven and earth fall into darkness. If you do not seek it within yourself, how could you obtain it from another? Before a single thought arises, all is complete;
the moment the tongue moves, error is committed. If Bodhidharma had not come from the West, Shaolin would have remained empty with its wall-gazing face.
The Second Patriarch sought peace of mind; he cut off one of his own arms. Water and milk have never been distinguished, yet the king of geese selects and eats them.
To return it to a man of exceeding measure, he must exert all his strength to draw it forth. Have you not seen that our Patriarch, the Sleeping Tiger, once spoke these words?
I cut off Master Sheng’s entanglements; I laugh until the nodding boulder falls over. This vast and great tradition must be upheld with strength;
do not waste away the days and months in vain.
To the Chan practitioner traveling to Tiantai, Yantai, and Siming:
The peaks of Mount Tiantai are so high they cannot be climbed; when climbing, hold fast to the mountain-shape staff. The Dragon Pool is so deep it cannot be measured;
when measuring, one must use a bottomless bowl. With the mountain-shape staff and the bottomless bowl, you, O superior man, can personally master them.
Holding it up: at the river’s edge, the jade-like tips of the plum branches have just begun to break open; by the stream, the eyes of the willows are now just starting to unfurl their green.
Before one’s very eyes, each thing reveals true wisdom; yet in this world’s turmoil, who is able to know it? Let me ask Cold Mountain: where did you inscribe these verses?
The wind-bell chimes clearly in the lofty trees; before the pavilion stand two *udumbara* flowers. The yellow monkeys, clutching their young, have all stolen them away.
One more search for the *nāgārjuna* flower—has his slumber yet awakened? Wrapping his head in the *kāṣāya*, he opens his eyes but cannot see his own nose.
At the edge of the cliff, the hanging spring pours forth inexhaustibly; shouting into the void, he hurls stones that drift like frost and snow. When will there be an appointment to emerge?
Shanlai comes; he tramples the black dragon until its two horns snap. He makes Changting Qici laugh to his heart's content.
His bag is filled with dry excrement.
[This is] sent for Vinaya Master Lian to travel to Mount Tai and Mount Yan.
The Wayman traveled to Mount Tiantai and likewise ascended Mount Yandang. At dawn he gazed upon the waterfalls; when night fell, he stayed at Fangguang Monastery.
In the empty pools dragons and snakes slumbered; along the narrow paths giant pythons coiled. Yet Tanyou simply sat in meditative repose, while Jueluo came and went as usual.
Supernatural powers are but a minor vision; how could the Buddha-dharma be something to deceive? From beneath your feet, mists and clouds arise; in the great void, sun and moon shine bright.
When the myriad phenomena surround them, the blue sky must be struck with a staff. This journey is truly magnificent; even at a hundred years, it would not be in vain.
When we meet again another day, his eyebrows shall surely be bristling upward.
A verse for the Chief Seat’s visit to see his mother:
In the past, Muzhou used to weave *pú* grass; At the two meal times, his strength was sufficient for the rice and gruel. Now that a man from Jiahe has come, he presses him until he is broken.
His feet—enduring pain, he could not sit in the full lotus posture. No sooner had he entered the gate of Xuefeng than his staff swallowed up heaven and earth.
Walking, he rode a jade horse; barefoot, he ascended Mount Kunlun. The Eye and Mind of humanity and heavens are like this; the heavens and earth of past and present are all alike.
Returning suddenly from three thousand miles away, the hen and chick peck and hatch at the same moment. We shall meet again another day.
Meeting him, he clapped his hands and sang of the spring breeze: "The void is shattered in a single blow; the great earth leaves no trace.
He saw off Attendant Mian, who had stayed one night at Yongjia before remaining at Caoxi. "Mian has been at my side for three years as a monk; indeed, Buddhas and Patriarchs are not the same."
The Path: Casting aside the old ruts of the past, he further paints a bull’s head in five colors; dotting its forehead with gold, he boasts of his skillful hand.
Such a character emerges spontaneously from nature, worthy to continue the lineage of the Muni’s descendants. When the myriad functions cease, the eyes rest upon the brows;
though a thousand sages do not carry it, both elbows are revealed. What was the matter with Xiangyan at that time? Suddenly—this!
To speak of "accomplishing faults" is to be remiss; Shushan would not consent, yet I myself do. Why wait for Xiangyan to open his mouth again?
Exhort Chan to go back and present this to him; it will not be like Shushan, who invited a bout of retching.

Seeing Vinaya Master Yun return to his retirement in Siming from Yunyan, I have incurred a debt of verses amounting to thousands and tens of thousands; from the beginning of the year to its end, I have written with such haste that the characters are indistinguishable.

These phrases and non-phrases—each and every one must be scrubbed away from the very beginning. Examine and deliberate with meticulous care; how could such a person be considered one who has finished the task?

On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, they will only find their hands and feet flailing in confusion. It would be better to be like Master Xinghua, who cuts things off immediately as soon as it is time to cut.
A great club strikes Ke-bin; he is fined and driven out of the monastery. Although this is like treating a dead horse, there is a transformative pivot within it.
Those students of Chan who come after should clearly grasp this koan; apply yourself with vigor and brilliance, and do not allow yourself to be turned by others.
It is like crossing the vast deep blue ocean, going straight to the other shore. The Persian from the South Sea recites the Eightfold Path;
the bearded man from the Western Heaven comes to the True Dawn.
Master Xuanzang seeks to enter the mountains to pitch his hermitage.
A man of the Way came from Mount Zhongfeng, saying he was a native of Jinhua. Amidst the dense and tangled *tao* trees, he once cultivated the causes for becoming a Great Being (*Mahāsattva*).
Having no money to buy clothes, he mended his tattered robes; regardless of whether others were rich or poor, he remained indifferent to their status.

With pine and vines for his hermitage and thorny shrubs for his door, he warmed his knees with yellow leaves while fierce beasts grew tame before him. "The Tathāgata’s Eye of True Dharma weighs seven or eight *jin* on either side"—at times...
A single blind man: the great earth is without a speck of dust. Cease dwelling in the futile hope that it is unattainable; how much more so for Hanshan, Shide, and Master Liaowang Baozhi?
Upon seeing him, they join their palms in diligent reverence; yet they must further cast down the broken rope of worldly entanglement held in their hands.
"Having captured the five-colored celestial qilin, the Master transmits [this teaching] so that those seeking it may listen to the Dharma and request instruction from the Head Seat Nan-sou.
I observe that this explanation is as clear as the sun; every word issues from the mouths of the people present. Buddha-nature is naturally and originally manifest."

Accomplished. Directly comprehending and clearly realizing, one transcends ten billion worlds. Reciting the sutras, reciting the Buddha’s name, and further reciting the Dharma, the radiance spreads day and night, illuminating all lands as numerous as motes of dust.
One turns over and ascends directly to the white lotus flower; though the soiled garments still cling to the body, they have not yet been cast off.

For a man of spirit, studying the Way values fierce and sharp resolve. The gate of skillful means opens, achieving the second stage. Dust and defilements are swept away by the thousands; the Unconditioned is revealed.

The ultimate meaning of the limits: when phenomena and phenomena are perfectly accomplished, and mind and mind are all fully complete, one sits at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas—six times six makes thirty-six.
This is called the true Dharma-offering to the Tathāgata. At this moment of letting go over the precipice, the Old Man of Nan personally attests to it;
thus, it is not hindered that wind and thunder arise from beneath the tongue.
To Shiyuan the Attendant: (This refers to the karmic occasion where Qingshan asked Deshan a question; Dayu Zhi said, "Qingshan only looked ahead and did not look behind.
When Emperor Tianhuang Longtan spoke thus, he had already entered the weeds before the question was even asked. Deshan’s staff was not applied in vain;
one would have no place to seek it even if one’s bones were ground to powder. Since Qingshan looked ahead and did not look behind, how could he have known how to leap up and hide?
The Northern Dipper: Great Fool, adding frost upon snow. Extending the hand that plays with the pearl of the azure dragon—this "head-word" has long remained unrecognized by anyone.
All say that Deshan’s functional skill was subtle; who knew that the Great Matter should be thus? Through this power, one realizes sainthood and transcends the mundane.
Yuanchan served me at Fufou; he once took these words and questioned them in detail. [He] pressed and constrained [me].
He instructs him to seek where he has sunk; a lacquered black bamboo whisk is gripped directly before his face. Now, each is situated in a different quarter of the sky;
suddenly, one comes beside him with incense in his sleeve. Taking up these words once more to bring them forth, the golden mane is vigorously tossed back at will.

The Chan Master Dao-ren has come from the Celestial Palace to preach the Dharma for the Senior Seat-holder Yi as he returns to Yunmen in Yuezhou. His tongue rolls forth like rolling thunder and lightning; the jagged peaks of the Double Emei Mountains stand as his sword of wisdom.
His emerald-like eyes turn and open with divine clarity; his sharp, penetrating wit cannot be touched by Mārajit, and his wondrous words claim him as a peer of the heavens.
People are suspicious. A blue hawk sweeps through the grass, startling foxes and rabbits; a noble steed lies hidden in its stall, making the dull mules tremble.

In years to come, when you sit upon the great throne, the myriad phenomena shall surround you. As the Buddha-sun is about to set, it should shine forth once more. The eyes of a patch-robed monk are truly like this;
if they were not so, why would they be? An iron staff upon his shoulder sprouts two wings; suddenly, in a moment of reflection, he crosses the green mountains and knocks at the door.

Leaving me in haste, you hurried away; on the river road, the frosty wind bore a chilling hue. The six temples of Yunmen reflect one another, their mountain colors and stream reflections most exceptionally sublime.
Upon the Heshang Lake, there are white lotuses; beholding them, my mind is purified and my eyes are likewise cleansed.
Do not grant this word; Dongshan knows it well. The scenery of today is not what it was of yore.
Had today been as it was back then, perhaps he would not have composed the verse on "not returning."
In the same rhyme, I see off Vinaya Master Lian as he travels to Lake Dongting:
The waters and mountains of Dongting are deep and secluded; Within the mountains, the falling leaves herald the high autumn. Before the doors of the people’s homes, pear and orange trees are planted;
With many pears and ripe oranges, there is no worry throughout the year. Jade halls and Buddhist temples stand side by side; Below them lies the Silver Three [Mountains].
Ten thousand acres of water; the Vulture Peak and Mount Penglai are not easily ascended. This place is truly a realm of immortals.

The fisherman appears and disappears, forgetting near or far; idly in his hand, he reels in the line. Who would know of Fan Li’s worth when the state has departed? How could the scent of *cōng* grass recognize the face of Zhang Han?
Beside the reeds and beneath the willows, he strikes the sounding oar; at the wave’s crest, a pair of sand gulls are startled up. Having caught a fish...
Entering the market to buy wine for drinking, he fell drunk and was unaware that the cold waves were pounding him. When Master Lu preached the Dharma, devas and humans came;
the square pond surged with water and lotus flowers bloomed. To this day, his remaining image inspires awe; one who bows at its feet dares not let a speck of dust startle it.
This departure of the Zen practitioner is truly worthy of praise. Wearing straw sandals and carrying a bamboo staff, he ascends through the clouds.
As the path turns and the peaks recede, no person is seen; a single long cry resounds through the thousand forests. I speak these coarse words because the Zen practitioner does not delight in them.
Though you have departed, your intent for Zen is sincere. I am neither going nor staying now; this poem is not composed, yet Zen is not absent.
[The Master] set aside two characters to await those who would come later.
He saw off Head Seat Duangiang and Abbot Yuejiang on their journey to Jiangxi.
"Bodhidharma did not come to the Eastern Land; every household has salt but no vinegar. The Second Patriarch did not go to the Western Heaven; his straw sandals..."
The ears are severed, yet no one pierces them. The Buddha is not the Buddha, and the Patriarch is not the Patriarch.

This Way is as clear as day, yet as base as soil. Who is it that mounts form upon sound? Let me count them for you from the beginning once more. Who says "Ma Boji"? Hanging a goat to sell dogs—no one knows.
A single roar of majestic authority leaves the world deaf for three days; the ears remain, as before, nothing but two pieces of skin. Who...

A Poem on the "White-Handed Robber": The Buddha-dharma is not something that can be grasped through intellectual understanding. Daoyu struck him three times under the ribs. Cooked rice must still come from within the grain.
Since ancient times, there have been many such Dharma-caves in Jiangxi. Now, as for this story—how truly is it?
If you do not believe me, go and look upon the rocks at the summit of Mount Wulao; there is nothing there but the entanglements of vines spreading north and south of the mountain.
This is Chan Master Duanjiang En, who succeeded Chan Master Hengchuan Gong;
and Chan Master Yuejiang Yin, who succeeded Chan Master Huya Fu.
Sent to escort Attendant Dai back to Tiantai, with a brief message for Chan Master Dongyu.
The home mountain is good, the home mountain is good. Steep cliffs and perilous peaks divide the path for birds. Never having come before, now there is no returning;
only the old man of Hanshan knows this heart. When composing poetry, Hanshan used no titles; he dwelt in secluded solitude upon the roots of pines on the rocks.
Where the golden oriole cries, white clouds fly; when the yellow leaves fall, he sings a song. He has lived his life in leisurely idleness.
Opening the mouth: "Dudud! Three hundred proposed titles; who indeed knows the definitive true sound? Ancient, it does not precede; now, it does not follow.
In this Jambudvīpa, the mountain of self and others: for those above, it is extremely easy; for those below, it is difficult.
Go and speak with the stones by the stream; on another day, come back again to form a heart-friend."
Regarding the lines "The golden oriole and the white clouds," this old man surely rejoiced in them himself;
thus, he unconsciously repeated them. Yet, as for the lines that follow, they are distinct once more—this may be called "vitality."
The monk who was sent to Yongjia came to Dongchan in the eighth month; now, at the start of spring, he has again purchased a boat for Dongjia. His longing to return is as fervent as this;
surely he will not have wasted his sandals in vain. Yongjia once stayed at Caoxi—how could such noble character be without its reward?

The human continuum continues; counting grains of sand and pouring them into the sea is but a waste of effort. It would be better to simply sing the song of returning home. Cease dwelling [in this state], for the stone bowl has long since been broken.
Last night, who was there to receive the transmission? When it is mended and made whole again in years to come, it will be filled with white rice and used to feed dogs.
Seeing off Chan Master Ken on his way to the Great Capital:
Chan Master Ken does not affirm himself, nor does he affirm others; he affirms only the Buddhas and the Patriarchs. This principle is difficult to explain in full detail.
In days of yore, Old Shao Shan was once questioned about the cause of his many words. Without concealing a single phrase, he swallowed the red flesh-body.
Do not dwell where such a capacity does not exist; I am merely moved by your diligent inquiries. Whenever I sit in the Hall of the Floating Buddha, the lions startle with their growls and sighs.
The myriad phenomena of the universe and all things dissolve and return to the One True Reality. Seven blows face thirteen; eight taels are but half a catty.

Clearly and luminously, there is no mutual confusion; distinctly, the host and guest are distinguished. This morning you took leave of me with words, now you go to tread upon the dust of the imperial capital.

Exhort yourself to study well; what you have attained shall be renewed daily. You should pay homage to the master who conferred the empowerment, forgetting both fatigue and hardship for the sake of the Dharma.
Do not merely indulge in empty words, lest you vainly squander the springtime of your life.
Bestowing the Title "Master of the Lone Cloud" upon Head Seat Mao of Lusan:
In days of yore at Lingxiao Peak, he frequently preached the Dharma at night within the celestial palaces. Three hundred, five hundred—what a bustling scene!
For their sake, he opened the eyes of the blind and the ears of the deaf. The lone cloud appears and disappears without intent; when will it come here to this green [mountain]?
Amidst the mountains, several songs of high melody resound as azure clouds close together; looking down, the myriad realms are but empty red dust. The green pines still recognize the gentleman of Lu;
the white stones surely bear the traces of the people of Qin. Sitting long upon the bamboo bed, I incline my two ears; above and below are blocked by the howling of mournful winds.
In years past, the martial energy of kings filled these valleys; one can imagine that even the grasses and trees were all heroes. Thus it is through ages both past and present.

The affairs of dreams are such as these; why not step lightly and roam through the empty caves? Draw from the spring to brew tea for a moment’s laughter, yet once you step out the door, you are already on the eastern side of the mountain.
The King of Astrology, Songchai, brought a verse by Venerable Dongzhou seeking a response:
"The Three Buddhas of the Past, Present, and Future share one single nature; All moving and sentient beings possess nothing more than this.
If you say that a dog has no Buddha-nature, You have lost the very life of Zhaozhou. If you have not yet attained the point of entry, you must give rise to deep reflection. Suddenly—
Breaking through the prison gates, he wears high upon his person the true seal of Vairocana. Sealing mud, sealing water, and sealing space, there is nowhere that is not correct.
Above, he does not long for the sages; below, he does not prize his own spirit. Those born under the *Ren* and *Kui* stems belong to Water;

they do not fear the "hair-tip star. Flowers bloom in the twelfth month; winter carries out the mandate of spring. In the Pine Hermitage, one directly receives and maintains [the truth]; all phenomena...
Naturally pure.
Send this message to the Chan practitioner at Nanping:
simply believe that you yourself are the Buddha. In all places, everything is the original truth. The peak of Mount Sumeru is high; the sun stands out clearly.
Noon. Amidst the wind-blown dust at the bottom of the great ocean, one does not consort with the myriad dharmas; such a person is truly one who dwells in ease.
If you pass before the Hall of the Mirror of the Source, a single shout must distinguish host from guest.
The path of practice for those on the Chan way is shown to be like a lotus flower: it does not cling to mud or water from the start, nor does it have any other [nature].
Like a king’s precious sword held in his hand, it completely cuts through all demons and heterodoxies. One must know that one's own Buddha and ancestors are also manifest in this very life.
Fellow seeker! What is this towering and majestic presence? It stands ten thousand fathoms high, like a precipitous cliff.
While everywhere else employs cremation, here I am simply buried alive. With a single sitting, I have cut it off at the source; how could I allow myself to be arranged by others?
This treasury of spiritual powers and radiant light—its enjoyment is perfectly harmonious. Chan Master Man has thus exhausted and penetrated the teaching; these are the true words of Xiujue.
Sending off the Head Seat Jue to travel to the Capital:
he goes, yet truly does not go; his single staff is cast from living iron. He comes, yet truly does not come; ancient paths before the gate grow with verdant moss.
Amidst a vast expanse of smoke and dust stretching for thousands of miles, the white sun shines upon the Golden Terrace. At the crown of his head—
Once the eye is correct, the mountain of self and others shall be toppled. In a single stroke, forty-nine peaks are leveled; they are gathered together and then released again.
Thus, the pivot of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is not encompassed by words. When the wind blows, the grass bows; clouds and thunder arise everywhere.
For a man of great purpose to travel on foot is like this: from Yan-nan to Ji-bei, how truly vast and far-reaching it is! Were Deshan and Linji to hear of this—
Rejoicing, he beheld him and praised him, saying: "This is truly the legitimate son of the Dharma King.

He is one who can unfurl the tridents and armor of the Three Mysteries, array the lords and ministers of the Five Ranks, and wield the great talent of the blazing furnace—something that neither heaven nor earth can rival. How extraordinary! How extraordinary!"
Sending off the Master of the Precious Treasury to roam West Lake:
How high is heaven? How thick is the earth? North, south, east, and west, they run in packs; they fill the void until not a single pit remains.
He pours out three hundred pecks of divine pearls; taking them does not precede his advance, and relinquishing them does not lag behind.
Not a single thing is brought forth—whom can one call empty-handed? Fragrant red cassias drift ten li across the lake;
on a small skiff, he sells water chestnuts and lotus roots.
Sending off Chan Practitioner Kwon to visit Dongcheon:
The ancestral Way has no past or present; the four sevens and two threes are difficult to enumerate.

Suddenly there emerges a three-legged donkey, which tramples the void until not an inch of soil remains. The eyebrows above the eyes stand upright as a pair, pouring out the clarity of the Yellow River.
Wait but a moment, and I shall overturn it all for you; to wash the Buddha-sun clean is truly not difficult.

Skillfully employ the mind in all places, and neither Buddhas nor Patriarchs can fathom it, while gods and humans are at a loss. Within the great chiliocosm of dust-motes, there is not even a hair’s breadth;
eighty-four thousand winds pass by like a breeze through the ear. Total darkness is total brightness; such is the natural law, yet it is not so at all. Barefoot and carrying it upon one's shoulders.
Running on without rest, one raises the head and bumps into one's own home. A-he-he! From antiquity to the present, what can be done about it?

For Guest Manager Zong: Heaven has no gates; earth has no doors. North, south, east, and west—what numbering could there be? A single phrase applied at the opportune moment is a precipice ten thousand fathoms high.
The Three Mysteries point out paths of a thousand differences: beneath the grass one seizes a soaring falcon; atop the tree a cool rabbit runs; upon the water rolls the dust of the reeds.
Across the great earth there is not a single inch of soil. Calling out to one another, they go to drink tea. Remember this: the sun is exactly at its zenith.
Sending off the Librarian Xun back to Jiangxi, following the rhyme of Master Yishan:

The mountains are high and the waters are far; ascending steeply, one faces the pure. This is a ready-made phrase; there is no need for hesitation. Breaking through a single speck of dust, a great scripture emerges.
Cutting through a thousand differences according to the capacity and depth of the occasion. The Tathāgatas of the three periods need not deliberate; hand-in-hand, we walk together.
His conduct was beyond compare; sitting and cutting off heaven and earth, he was a man of the highest caliber.

Not a single drop remained of West River’s water. Baizhang ascended once more to Mazu’s hall; the precious sword at his head radiated its brilliance. With a single roar of awe-inspiring power, the ten thousand phenomena were struck with terror;
even now, monks suffer the calamity of it. Hearing Huangbo’s grandmotherly heart, one’s tongue stutters in shock. How could this compare to the undifferentiated whole?
It cannot be split apart; beyond three thousand miles, there is no one to raise it.
To the Zen student Xian, I show this:
to advance is to study the Way, and to retreat is to establish one's character. Only when the myriad functions have all ceased is one the person of original nature. Gather ten...

Counting thunderclaps as a single shout need not trouble one in manifesting the Linji school’s style. Taking hundreds of thousands of suns as a single illumination, Dongshan’s precious mirror still involves a speck of dust.
Do not fall into the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials; cease dividing the Five Ranks of Sovereign and臣 (Minister).
A team of iron hammers without holes runs forth; one that enters the gate weighs a thousand pounds.
O Zen practitioner, upon entering the gate you must distinguish the host; the mud and water were divided at that very moment. Having no leisure to speak a word, who can discuss this in detail?
Do not mistake the Eye of the True Dharma for a broken sand bowl; you should be like a ten-year-old colt that leaps in a single bound onto Mount Kunlun.
Lofty within the triple world, where would you not be honored as supreme?

In sending off the Zen practitioner Wén, these words are not ornate and the ultimate principle is not flowery. When the samādhi of actual practice is manifest, how could it require elaborate explanation? The blue sky is vast and clear, and the myriad phenomena are revealed;
the bright moon shines through the night upon a thousand homes. Without a contrived mind, one naturally accords with the Way; if there is a vow, one does not scatter sand.

"Traveling east does not depart from the benefit of traveling west. When asked about the Buddha’s answer regarding the three catties of hemp, [Dongshan] sent Xian as *karmadāna* back to the mouth of the White Clouds on Mount Tiantai, saying:
"Who would dare say this is not good? This talk is truly not so; do not seek it within the words.
Like the jewel within a king’s topknot, only upon obtaining it does one realize it is a treasure. Venerable Tian’ai Xian, the *vina*, was no ordinary person in his resolve;

he traveled extensively at the gates of the patriarchs, yet he regrets that he did not begin sooner. He mistook the elder brother’s wife for his own, only to find out she was actually his sister-in-law.
On this journey back to my native land, I shall go to inquire of the old man of Hanshan. With yellow leaves filling the steps before him, it is precisely the path by which I came.

While viewing the waterfalls amidst Mount Yanlang with the Chan practitioner Xuan, the entire body of the iron walls and silver mountains was revealed; pressed forth from the tip of the staff, it emerged.
Come! Verses for a parting gift from the south, north, east, and west. Yesterday I ascended the Floating Buddha Hall; I do not say where I have come from.
My crown is bowed and my eyes open wide; with the fearless lion’s roar, I have startled the blind donkey to its fall and trampled the old turtle’s nose to death.
Summon Li Dagon of the eastern village to pull away the tea wheel for me!
Sending off Chan person An to return to Dongchan to visit his teacher:
Your teacher Huangbo was no concern of mine. Letting go in two places and casting aside in three; "Ding" for one and "Zhuo" for two.
He reveals the True Person of No Rank and twists the very nose of the patch-robed monk. It is not that it is not so, nor that it is so; to cut through iron and sever nails, you must realize it.
Grasping. Yanruo lost his head in the mirror; Layman Xue caught the moon in the water. One phrase settles heaven and earth;
a great staff strikes the rat. Laughing until he collapses under Bimoye’s staff, he returns to Dongshan to present it to the Master.
Who can entrust this golden circle and thorny plum?
The cobbler Pi Sheng sought the patriarch’s legacy:
a single sandal left behind. Scorched by the sun and buffeted by the wind, it is beyond compare. Sometimes it is cut into seven or eight pieces, yet it remains whole when stitched back together.
Through the needle-holes and the paths of the thread, the work of the Buddha is accomplished; in every moment and every mote of dust, it is proclaimed.
This meaning is not merely that beneath the feet of a patch-robed monk is not a place to let go of the body or sacrifice one’s life;
whether an inch long or a foot short, all have their function, and whether adding or subtracting, all are composed. The skillful means of the "skin-born" are even more subtle and dense;
this wondrous point is not like anything ordinary. When meeting [this], do not ask whether one has attained it or not; truly, every step transcends the mundane world. The Elephant King.
Kicking and trampling, he shakes heaven and earth; Mount Sumeru at the bottom of the sea is completely smashed by his shout.

Throughout all quarters, vast numbers proclaim him a master of the school, yet in the end, who can truly follow this model? Simply apply your effort to the task at hand; do not haggle over three coins or two coppers.

The Chan practitioner Prou seeking a field for planting and broad alms is truly difficult to find. He is not like that old thief Yangqi, whose skillful means of seizing food and driving the plow are lofty;
how could the Elder of Hunan have ever known him? The Chan practitioner Prou of Zhitang Lake Temple is one who transcends the standard and surpasses his lineage. How extraordinary!
How extraordinary! He receives [offerings] while playing with sand and dirt before the gate; with both hands he supports the plow while the water rises above his knees.

With earnest devotion, he seeks the verse from the Elder Xiujue. Xiujue suffers from muteness and is further afflicted by deafness. At times, he speaks a single phrase offhand, which fills the great earth and transcends empty space.
Taking Mount Sumeru as a brush and the waters of the ocean as ink, he paints the Great Void into five colors. Intending to...
Selling it at the foot of the steps, Han Shan and Shi De were made to laugh until they fell over.
Former Head Seat Lin has returned to Muzhou to visit his kin;
yesterday he visited Huangbo. Outstanding within the monastic community, he possesses an ancient bearing that remains until now, filling the heavens with his great meaning.
Kun. At the ferry crossing, the waves still surge and crash. On Mount Mi, he closed his door to compile the *Qingpu*. He cooked rice to provide for his mother’s morning and evening meals.
Shao Yang once came to press him until his leg broke; who can now support this family tradition that has fallen to the ground?

Long ago on Mount Gu, he clarified this principle; "stealing food" and "driving the plow" cannot be compared to it. Suddenly bidding me farewell, he returned to Tian Tai, where the day-lily flourishes in the northern hall.
The fragrance of the grass rises with the breeze; in the depths of spring, there is a lingering intent to return. At the end of the branches, flowers must surely be blooming on every tree.
There is no need to further inquire about the waters of the Stone Bridge; let us simply walk back and forth together, hand in hand, regardless of their shallowness or depth.
Seeing off the Abbot Kuizang as he returns to travel to Tiantai and Yandangshan:
The hand of a man of the Way grips the sword of wisdom; Its wondrous function sweeps across all directions like a flash of lightning. Dongchan and Huqiu have no recourse but to watch him go;
He returns to Yandangshan and Tiantai to roam through their perils. Beneath the Stone Bridge, dragons coil and writhe; The gurgling sound of the western ravine startles the soul.
Tidal waves and billows—do not hesitate to take a single step and cut them off, lest all people of the great earth attempt to climb and grasp them. The dragon pool is deep and unfathomable;
the snowy waterfall overturns the void and the cloud-cave is black. Jueluo enters and exits without a fixed trace; if you wish to pursue him, where can you seek him?
Within the Tathāgatagarbha lies the maṇi jewel, its cold radiance shining brightly day and night. When meeting people...
He pours out a full measure; those with true knowledge naturally raise their eyebrows.
In this same rhyme, I present this to Censor Chen, who styles himself "Spring Field Ox.
This Spring Field Ox is none other than the Ox of Mount Wei; one simply must recognize this very head. The nostrils of the vast sky have nothing by which to be grasped.
Touching east, touching west—once full, simply rest. I now apply the whip and the halter for you; all former water and grass are swept away.
When you are so hungry that your skin wastes away and your bones are exposed, you will still have two horns upon your head as before.
Presented to Yao Xisheng, who is skilled in *zǐpíng* (the calculation of fate):

A single melody from Shaozhou transcends both past and present; it does not belong to the notes of gong, shang, jiao, zhi, or yu. It is difficult to harmonize with either heaven or earth—there is only this:
the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. Having attained this, Zǐpíng is able to adapt and transform; he understands how to distinguish between the noble and the base.
Auspiciousness and misfortune—these distinct sounds have already been spread before the ears of men; how could they exist within the calculations and displacements of the Creator?
The Tathāgatas of the three periods have transmitted this melody; for forty-nine years, their singing was never enough. Yet not a single word can be proclaimed from beginning to end;
they merely hold up a flower branch to dazzle the eyes of men. Bodhidharma faced the wall for nine years, yet his desire to raise the chant remains unfulfilled. The snow is cruel.
Though the frost was cruel and he did not die of the cold, once dead, he suddenly spat forth the spring breeze.
An old man of Tongjiang, Yang Xisheng—his disposition and orientation are both clear and distinct. Do not say he merely studied the arts of Zi Ping; he truly harmonizes with the melody of Shaoxiang.
As the Master of the Virtue-Treasury departs, black winds whirl rain that strikes the *laṅgān* bamboo. Hail and sleet shatter the plantain altar. Hanshan claps his hands and Shide laughs;
one merely perceives the surging billows beneath one’s eyes. Why are the eyes of this practitioner so azure? A *maṇi* jewel shines upon his palm.
The red sun shines upon the ocean of three thousand worlds; fish, turtles, and giant whales emerge with their heads and horns bared.
Do not waste your lifelong efforts on such crooked things. On the hook at the end of the fragrant bait, right and wrong are distinguished.

Letting go and drawing in—just leave it as it is. In the end, the water is cold and they do not eat. *Maṇi* jewel, *maṇi* jewel! Do not let the black dragon of the seabed recognize it. At that time, when facing...
I do not understand or appreciate this; I have been called a "white-handed thief" by others.
Following the verses on the Dharma-talks and general discourses (pǔshuō) of Chan Master Chijue, I compose these verses based on the karmic conditions presented within those general discourses.
The deluded old man preaches the Dharma like clouds and rain; what flows from his mouth is entirely water. You should know that this water has no time of exhaustion;
its vast waves submerge the void and have not yet ceased. The five Mount Sumerus smile and nod their heads; the ten thousand phenomena listen with their ears pricked up.
Among those who are forceful and enduring, none surpass this patch-robed monk; seeing this, one’s hair and bones must stand on end. — *Yuzimuzi* (Admonition to Mother and Son)
The chick pecks and the hen pips at the same moment; once it passes through the faculty of hearing, joy is awakened. Sentient emotions and sensory dust entwine, flowing freely in all directions.
Whether worldly conditions are adverse or favorable, every single thing is the Way. What, then, is this "mind" and what is this "Way"? How much more so when one further divides them into one and two?

Great wisdom is perfectly luminous, opening wide the crown of the head. These expedient means are merely pointed out according to the capacity of beings. Lord Jing possessed a temperament that was both firm and grand; he was... [the text trails off].
Because he was so resolute and great, he questioned the Buddha’s intent; though the Elder did not answer, he remained even more intimate [with him].

His words were elegant in style and complete in meaning. At that time, what could Master Wen have done? The more he struck at it, the more the obstacles blazed. When the Way exists, it is seen through direct observation, casting off all fetters.
With one stroke, two segments are severed, revealing fierce acuity. He further relished the simple and austere life like a *dhūta* practitioner—this is truly the foremost among men.
A single meaning. Ziyan Kunzhongxian was both wise and enlightened; his loyalty, righteousness, and literary talent were peerless in the world.

He diligently repaid his mother’s virtue, and his request for the Dharma from Old Qian was not easily granted. "Zhaozhou’s dog has no Buddha-nature"—this one phrase cuts off the very source and dissolves all traces.
At that moment, the mountains, rivers, and the great earth became empty; the self’s numinous clarity had nowhere to cling. Mihu...

His two eyes are like flashes of lightning; responding to stimuli and engaging with beings is like a playful game. Since he was already able to take up his brush and demarcate empty space, why did he fail to recognize Attendant Wang?
A lion has always known how to bite people; Hanlu’s chasing of clods of earth was merely a futile attempt at deliberation.
To suddenly realize it is not difficult: an octagonal millstone dwells in the void. I observe this Dharma taught by the Elder of Folly;
it is like seasonal rain soaking the great earth, moistening all things—fine and coarse, long and short—each sprouting forth according to its own capacity.
I bow my head and compose this verse in praise, so that we may together realize the fundamental wisdom of this Elder throughout kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Always manifest before you. Do not allow the character "yuan" (元) to remain in your breast by any means.
As for the characters to be excised, they shall await future generations.
Written by Master Hedongyu as an instruction to Librarian Zang.
The ancestral hall stands solitary, yet radiates brilliance; for a thousand years and more, the ancient style endures.
A single phrase, whole and undivided, cannot be split asunder—it is cast into the sea of a thousand or ten thousand people. The Great Void does not admit the slightest stain of dust;
at the head of the sutra, one finds no one to question. Placing hands together at the breast, one asks: "What? Not knowing a single character, one remains humble; such is the presence of true skill.
To have no skillful means is merely to scratch an itch through a boot. How can this compare to a single arrowhead piercing the three barriers, severing hundreds of thousands of idle delusions?
It makes that old fellow Dongshan laugh to his heart’s content;
his thoroughgoing, bone-chilling, and pure wind not only removes the torment of suffering and heat, but directly opens the eyes and ears of the entire world.

Master You, the Librarian, visited me as a seeker of the Way at Mount Lingxiao. He knocked upon my gate beneath the pines; when I opened it, I beheld his countenance. His laughter and speech were as warm as the spring breeze.
In human life, encounters are rare; I am moved by the sincerity of this bond of righteousness. How shall I expound the Way of the Patriarchs? Do not judge it by words or traces.
"Setting out at dawn, he went forth; barefoot, he ascended Mount Kunlun.
This verse likely refers to the time when [Songchun] first met the Master. Thereafter, he followed him from time to time.
He was rarely separated from [the Master’s] side. When I was at Baoning, he served as the Head Seat (zuòyuán). I observed that his character was exceedingly sincere and earnest;
both his learning and his skills in calligraphy and dyeing were excellent. His name was Liángyóu, and his style name was Zhòngmóu.

He left the monastery to reside at Wúxiǎng in Lìshuǐ, and now resides at Xiānyán in Wēnzhōu, where he serves as the Dharma heir to our Master. This is indeed the lineage from which he comes, beginning with...
Indeed it is so.

Amidst this boat, I am moved by the realization that my life is nearing its twilight years; all worldly affairs have vanished from my thoughts. Dwelling in seclusion beside the deep forest, I look back and cast off the fetters of the mundane world.
Gazing at the clouds, I sing aloud; facing the moon, I sometimes clap my hands. Riding the wind, I cross gullies and ravines; sitting, I listen to the resonance of the pines.
Resting my head on a stone, I mock Xu You; waving my hand, I decline Yuan Hao. Why do I engage in this journey of service? Merely bowing and looking up in pursuit of worldly things.
My solitary figure is like a drifting duckweed, tossed and fluttering in the wind. Having come here to roam the rivers and seas, I propel my light oars through the waves.
At dawn, I eat the morning air as my meal; at night, I lodge upon the rising tide. The boatman brushes away the early frost, while flying snow sprinkles upon his head.
The new year still holds lingering cold; the rising sun illuminates the myriad phenomena. Tomorrow morning I shall reach Mount Kuanglu; this is enough to console my refined appreciation.
The title reads: "Reflections While Aboard the Boat. Thus it is said: All affairs vanish from one’s expectations, and one merely bows and looks up at the passing things.
As for the verse beginning with "Upon arriving at Mount Kuanglu in the early morning," was it perhaps composed when he was responding to the summons to Yongfu?
Furthermore, there is a piece written while traveling to Fanyi, requesting a boat to reach Chikou, which was composed due to being detained by the wind;
because the manuscript copy contains numerous errors, I have not included it here.
In the same rhyme, I send off Chan Master Chi, the Head Seat, on the fifteenth day of the third month.
A stone tiger from the Southern Mountain: two or three are not one. The fish are thick and the net is dense; let them go and bring them back.
What method is there? To cleave open Linji’s Three Mysteries, to blindfold the single eye at the crown of the head, to drum forth the clouds and thunder upon the mountain of ignorance,
and to crash the lightning amidst the sea of afflictions— not only do the Buddhas of the three periods, the six generations of patriarchs,
and the old monks of the world tremble with fear and have their souls startle, but it also causes all those with hair and fur to lose heart and all roots of goodness to be destroyed.

The vessels and sentient beings—each eye askew, each nose straight. This is what is called preaching the Dharma in the celestial palaces, transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations.
Beholding the majesty of the elephant-dragon, heaven and earth seem far too narrow.
In this verse, I send off He Xitang:
he has clearly brought forth the Master of Masters. What need is there to strike the drum of Leimen? To grasp the meaning before the sound is in vain;
to master it after the phrase is no true patch-robed monk. He reveals hundreds of thousands of gates of samādhi, amidst which elephants, dragons, and foxes jostle together.
